question: What is the biggest danger when a young child has acute watery diarrhoea?

options.A: Rapid loss of body fluids and electrolytes
options.B: Permanent damage to the intestinal lining
options.C: Complete loss of appetite for solid food

explanation: You nailed it! When a child has watery diarrhoea, water and vital salts rush out of the body very quickly, which can lead to dangerous dehydration. Catching this early makes all the difference!

question: Why does severe dehydration eventually cause organs to stop working in a child?

options.A: Electrolyte imbalances cause immediate paralysis of the heart
options.B: The kidneys stop working because they are overworked by toxins
options.C: Reduced blood volume leads to poor oxygen delivery to tissues
options.D: The digestive tract bursts from lack of internal pressure

explanation: Think of blood like a delivery truck carrying oxygen. When water is lost, total blood volume drops, meaning vital organs don't get the oxygen they need to keep running smoothly.

question: What is the main goal of giving Oral Rehydration Therapy (ORT)?

options.A: To stop the bowels from moving immediately
options.B: To replace lost fluids and electrolytes using the gut
options.C: To kill the bacteria causing the stomach infection
options.D: To provide full daily nutritional calories

explanation: Spot on! ORT uses the body's natural drinking process to safely put back all the water and essential mineral salts that were washed away.

question: How does adding a little glucose to oral rehydration solution help the body absorb water?

options.A: Glucose creates a thick barrier that stops water from leaving the body
options.B: Glucose binds with sodium to pull water across the gut wall together
options.C: Glucose makes the drink taste sweet so the child will drink more
options.D: Glucose feeds the good bacteria so they can repair the damaged bowel

explanation: It's like a team effort! Sodium and glucose hitch a ride together on the same transport protein. As glucose is absorbed, it pulls sodium and water right along with it into the bloodstream.

question: Which specific protein in the intestine makes Oral Rehydration Therapy work so well?
explanation: SGLT1 (sodium-glucose linked transporter type 1) is the hero protein! It links sugar and salt uptake in the small intestine to pull precious water into the body.

question: What is the big advantage of modern low-osmolality ORS compared to the older, stronger formula?

options.A: It reduces stool volume and the need for IV fluids
options.B: It provides all the daily vitamins a growing child needs
options.C: It tastes much sweeter and dissolves instantly in cold water
options.D: It cures bacterial infections without needing antibiotics

explanation: By lowering the sugar and salt slightly, the modern formula creates less osmotic pull in the gut, which means less watery stool and fewer trips to the hospital for drips!

question: Why did health experts lower the amount of sugar in the standard ORS formula over time?

options.A: To save manufacturing costs for pharmaceutical companies
options.B: To make the powder dissolve faster in contaminated water
options.C: To stop children from developing diabetes during illness
options.D: To prevent excess sugar from pulling extra water back into the gut

explanation: Too much sugar actually acts like a sponge, drawing water back out into the stool. Lowering the sugar keeps the fluid moving safely into the body instead!

question: A toddler is brought to the clinic with sunken eyes, fussiness, and drinks the ORS eagerly. How would you classify this dehydration?
explanation: You got it! Irritability, sunken eyes, and drinking eagerly are classic signs of moderate ('some') dehydration. Giving ORS right here in the clinic will help them bounce back.

question: Which of these clinical signs tells you a child has SEVERE dehydration?

options.A: Lethargy or floppiness and sluggish skin pinch
options.B: Restless behavior and dry oral mucosa
options.C: Eager and rapid drinking from a cup

explanation: When a child is very sleepy, floppy, or their skin pinch takes a long time to go back, that's a red flag for severe fluid loss requiring urgent medical help.

question: What happens if a caregiver mixes an ORS sachet in way too little water?

options.A: The child will refuse to drink because the solution is too cold
options.B: The extra salt crystals will kill all the bacteria in the stomach
options.C: The concentrated solution can worsen dehydration by drawing water into the gut
options.D: The medicine works twice as fast to stop the watery stool

explanation: Measurements matter! Too little water makes the drink too salty (hypertonic), which actually pulls body water out into the intestines and makes dehydration worse.

question: What is the best feeding item to use when giving ORS to an infant?

options.D: A plastic syringe with a needle

explanation: Always choose a clean cup and spoon! Baby bottles have narrow parts that are very hard to clean properly and can easily trap germs that cause more infections.

question: For how long should a child take zinc supplements after having acute diarrhoea?

options.B: Only until the stool is firm

explanation: Even if the child feels completely better after two days, completing the full 10 to 14 day course of zinc is vital to rebuild the gut lining and protect against future illness.

question: What is the main medical benefit of giving zinc supplements during childhood diarrhoea?

options.A: It instantly stops all vomiting within one hour
options.B: It replaces lost potassium in the bloodstream
options.C: It repairs the gut lining and shortens illness duration
options.D: It acts as a strong painkiller for stomach cramps

explanation: Zinc is wonderful for healing! It acts like medicine for the gut walls, helping them repair faster and boosting the child's immune system to clear the bug away.

question: Why is starting ORT right at home so important for community health?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any professional medical checkups
options.B: It prevents family members from catching the same stomach bug
options.C: It guarantees that the underlying viral infection will disappear overnight
options.D: It stops dehydration from progressing to a dangerous stage before reaching a clinic

explanation: Every minute counts! Giving fluids immediately at home stops mild fluid loss from turning into a life-threatening emergency before the family even reaches the hospital.

question: Which harmful traditional practice should nurses actively discourage when teaching mothers about diarrhoea?

options.A: Mixing ORS packets in clean drinking water
options.B: Withholding food and fluids to rest the bowel
options.C: Continuing to breastfeed the infant on demand
options.D: Giving zinc supplements for two full weeks

explanation: Never starve a tummy bug! Stopping food and water only makes malnutrition and dehydration worse. Children with diarrhoea need continued feeding and plenty of fluids to heal.
